name: Modern damage numbers
oneLiner: 2020s damage numbers: each hit arcs out of the target and lands, crits pop with a big overshoot, a burst and a short shake, rapid hits on one target roll into one punching total (12 → 47 → 83), every damage type has its own colour and a small procedural icon, misses and blocks are small words, big numbers stay on top, and nothing lands on another unit or the UI. Smooth bold sans on HD canvases, a crisp 1-bit raster on native pixel canvases. Replaces E-01 bouncing numbers (use one or the other).
notFor: games that hide HP on purpose (horror, realism sims)
a strict 8/16-bit period look where the old bouncing digits are the point (use E-01)
rhythm games (timing words are a different element)
hundreds of hits per second from many sources on one target (merging helps, but the screen still fills)

needs: hit event on the impact frame: {target, amount, kind: damage|crit|heal|shield|mp|miss|block|dodge|status, type: physical|fire|ice|shock|poison|arcane|heal|shield|mana}
target screen anchor: centre x and top of head y (above any HP bar)
frame clock in ms (world time that pauses during hit-stop)
optional: rectangles to avoid (banner, HUD, windows) and unit sprite rects with ids
provides: hit-stop request (ms) on the impact frame
screen shake and flash request for criticals
list of live pop rectangles (for other overlays to avoid)

assets: module/damage-pop.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_DamagePop): motion, merging, type colours and procedural icons, smooth and crisp text rasters, placement, drawing
no image, font or audio files (system sans stack, never loaded from the network)
